title: U.S. House · Florida's 3rd District
area: North-central Florida, including Gainesville and Ocala.

context.text: Incumbent Kat Cammack's Republican primary was canceled and she advanced unopposed. Seth Harp won the Democratic primary over three opponents.

candidates.name: Kat Cammack
candidates.ballotNote: Republican primary was canceled; advanced unopposed.

summary.text: Kat Cammack is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 3rd District, first elected in 2020. She grew up in Colorado, worked on Rep. Ted Yoho's 2012 campaign and then served nearly a decade on his staff, and later owned a marketing firm. Her congressional office says she serves on the Agriculture and Energy and Commerce committees.

background.text: Born in Denver, Colorado; according to her congressional office, she grew up on a cattle ranch outside Denver and took part in 4-H and local rodeo.

Earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Metropolitan State University of Denver (2015) and a master's degree in national defense and strategic studies from the U.S. Naval War College (2018).
Says that after being homeless for several months she was recruited in 2011 to join Ted Yoho's congressional campaign in Florida, and then managed his successful 2012 campaign.
Served for nearly a decade as deputy chief of staff to Rep. Ted Yoho, according to her congressional office.
Owned a marketing firm and describes herself as a small business owner before entering Congress.
Won the open Republican primary for Florida's 3rd District in August 2020 and the November 3, 2020 general election with 57.1% of the vote over Democrat Adam Christensen, succeeding Ted Yoho.
Re-elected in 2022 (over Danielle Hawk and Linda Brooks) and 2024 (over Tom Wells), after winning Republican primaries against Justin Waters and Alec Stevens.

In the 2025-2026 term, assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; and Health subcommittees) and the Committee on Agriculture. Her office says she chairs the Emerging Tech Task Force and co-founded the Republican Women's Caucus in 2025.
According to her congressional office, she is married to Matt, a Gainesville Fire Rescue firefighter/paramedic, and they have a daughter.

priorities.text: Health: says she is focused on lowering prescription drug prices and holding pharmaceutical companies accountable for price increases and industry consolidation.

Economy: as the only Floridian on the House Agriculture Committee, has run an in-person listening tour with Florida farmers and ranchers to shape Farm Bill provisions affecting the state's agriculture industry.

positions.summary: Praised the Trump administration's February 2026 revocation of the EPA's 'Endangerment Finding,' the legal basis for federal vehicle-emissions standards, framing the rollback of the underlying climate regulation as a win for lower prices and energy production.
positions.quote: 'GREEN NEW SCAM' up in smoke. The climate crowd said killing Obama-era emissions rules would wreck America. Instead? Cheaper cars. More energy. Less bureaucratic chokehold. America builds again.

candidates.name: Seth Harp
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over three opponents.

summary.text: Seth Harp is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 3rd District. He has worked for about 30 years in broadcast media as a host, anchor, reporter, director and operations manager, most recently at ESPN Gainesville. He won the August 2026 Democratic primary and describes a platform of Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid protection, term limits and child care relief.

background.text: Born in Auburn, Indiana; graduated from DeKalb High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Western Michigan University in 2001.
After college, stayed in Kalamazoo, Michigan, and became, in his words, one of the youngest hosts in the history of WKZO radio.
Moved to Florida over a decade ago to serve as Director of Programming and Host for iHeartMedia's Fox Sports Radio and Gator Radio affiliate in Jacksonville.
Has been Operations Manager for ESPN Gainesville (WRUF-AM) for about five years, as of his 2025 survey, and has taught as an adjunct at the University of Florida's College of Journalism.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Tom Wells, Troy Albers and George Hubac.
His Ballotpedia profile lists his religion as United Methodist; his survey describes a platform he calls the '13 Stripes of Strength', which includes a child care proposal he calls the C.U.B.S. Act.

priorities.text: Campaign platform titled '13 Stripes of Strength,' including a proposed child-care stipend program ('C.U.B.S. Act') rather than direct cash payments to have children.
Says elected officials should be held to character standards of responsibility, respect, integrity, kindness and honesty.

positions.summary: Proposes a 'Child Unity Break Stipend' to provide families relief on childcare costs, which he frames as a better use of resources than direct cash payments for having children.

summary.text: Mike Klein is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 3rd District. A fifth-generation Floridian raised in Gainesville, he is a West Point graduate and Army combat veteran who served from 1985 to 2003. He is chairman of Warrior Centric Health and is running on a platform of removing corporate and special-interest money from politics.

background.text: According to his campaign survey, he is a fifth-generation Floridian raised in Gainesville in the 1970s.
Graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1989 and later earned a graduate degree from the University of South Carolina's Darla Moore School of Business.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 2003; he says he was a Ranger-qualified Infantry officer in the 25th Infantry Division who led soldiers in combat in Operation Desert Storm.
Says he has worked and lived internationally, building expertise in international business, economic development, university innovation and entrepreneurship.

Co-founded and chairs Warrior Centric Health, which he says works to improve care for the military and veteran community; he says he started it after his brother, an Army infantry officer, lost limbs to an IED.
Is running as an independent; he describes himself as the father of two "Gators" and says he has pledged not to take corporate PAC or special-interest money.

priorities.text: Ending corruption and removing corporate PAC and special-interest money from politics.
Banning insider stock trading by members of Congress and ending gerrymandering.
Building an independent bloc in Congress to force bipartisan cooperation.
